claim: The study cohort consisted of 115 participants with HIV infection for at least 1 year who had been receiving ART for at least 0.9 years (median 9 years, interquartile range [IQR] 5.2–16.6).
source: This cross-sectional study evaluated 115 participants with HIV infection for at least 1 year and who had been receiving ART for at least 0.9 years (median 9 years, interquartile range [IQR] 5.2–16.6) (Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript directly reports the cohort size, inclusion criteria, and treatment duration with specific statistical measures.

claim: The study cohort was 77% male.
source: The study cohort was 77% male, 60% black, and median participant age was 45 years.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the percentage of male participants in the cohort.

claim: The study cohort was 60% black.
source: The study cohort was 77% male, 60% black, and median participant age was 45 years.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the racial composition of the cohort.

claim: The median participant age was 45 years.
source: The study cohort was 77% male, 60% black, and median participant age was 45 years.
evidence: The manuscript directly reports the median age of participants.

claim: The percentage of intact proviruses versus time on therapy exhibited a biphasic decay pattern.
source: When we examined a plot of percent intact proviruses versus time on therapy (Figure 1C), we observed a biphasic decay pattern, consistent with previous reports (Peluso et al., 2020; Gandhi et al., 2023; McMyn et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript describes a biphasic decay pattern observed in Figure 1C and cites previous reports supporting this finding.

claim: The best-fit model for percentage intact proviruses had decay slope changes at 1.6 and 9 years of ART.
source: Indeed, when we fitted piece-wise linear functions with allowances for up to two breaks, the best-fit model had decay slope changes at 1.6 and 9 years of ART.
evidence: The manuscript reports specific breakpoints identified through piece-wise linear modeling.

claim: The R2 score of a piece-wise linear model with two breaks was 44.18%, while the score for a linear model without any breaks was 16.3%.
source: The R2 score of a piece-wise linear model with two breaks was 44.18%, while the score for a linear model without any breaks was 16.3%.
evidence: The manuscript directly reports R2 scores for different models.

claim: In PWH within approximately 0–6 years of ART initiation, a significant proportion of the participants exhibited high fractions of intact proviruses (50–90%).
source: In PWH within approximately 0–6 years of ART initiation, a significant proportion of the participants exhibited high fractions of intact proviruses (50–90%).
evidence: The manuscript describes the distribution of intact provirus fractions in early ART participants.

claim: After approximately 6 years of ART, the majority of participants had reservoirs for which intact proviruses represented a minor fraction of the overall reservoir (0–30%).
source: After approximately 6 years of ART, however, the majority of participants had reservoirs for which intact proviruses represented a minor fraction of the overall reservoir (0–30%).
evidence: The manuscript describes the distribution of intact provirus fractions in long-term ART participants.

claim: Frequencies of CD4 and CD8 T naive cells were significantly negatively correlated with total HIV DNA frequency.
source: Frequencies of CD4 and CD8 T naive cells, as well as their expression of CD38, were significantly negatively correlated with total HIV DNA frequency, consistent with the hypothesis that larger reservoirs are associated with depletion of the naive T cell subsets and increased immune activation.
evidence: The manuscript reports negative correlations between naive T cell frequencies and total HIV DNA.

claim: Larger HIV reservoirs are associated with depletion of the naive T cell subsets and increased immune activation.
source: Frequencies of CD4 and CD8 T naive cells, as well as their expression of CD38, were significantly negatively correlated with total HIV DNA frequency, consistent with the hypothesis that larger reservoirs are associated with depletion of the naive T cell subsets and increased immune activation.
evidence: The manuscript infers this biological interpretation from observed correlations.

claim: CD4 and CD8 Tcm and Tem cells were weakly positively correlated with total HIV DNA.
source: In contrast, CD4 and CD8 Tcm and Tem cells were weakly positively correlated with total HIV DNA, possibly due to increased differentiation of the naive compartment into these memory subsets in people with larger reservoirs.
evidence: The manuscript reports positive correlations between memory T cell subsets and total HIV DNA.

claim: Increased differentiation of the naive compartment into memory subsets may occur in people with larger reservoirs.
source: In contrast, CD4 and CD8 Tcm and Tem cells were weakly positively correlated with total HIV DNA, possibly due to increased differentiation of the naive compartment into these memory subsets in people with larger reservoirs.
evidence: The manuscript speculates about a possible mechanism for the observed correlation.

claim: Markers of T cell activation and exhaustion were weakly but significantly positively correlated with total HIV DNA, including NKG2A+ CD4 T, PD-1+ CD4 T, HLA-DR+ CD4 T, PD-1+ CD8 T, and PD-1+/CCR7+ CD8 T frequencies.
source: Markers of T cell activation and exhaustion were weakly but significantly positively correlated with total HIV DNA, including NKG2A+ CD4 T, PD-1+ CD4 T, HLA-DR+ CD4 T, PD-1+ CD8 T, and PD-1+/CCR7+ CD8 T frequencies, among others (Table 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports positive correlations between activation/exhaustion markers and total HIV DNA, with reference to tables and figures.

claim: An inverse correlation with the CD4/CD8 T cell ratio was observed for both intact and total HIV DNA.
source: For both intact and total HIV DNA, an inverse correlation with the CD4/CD8 T cell ratio was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports an inverse correlation with reference to a figure.

claim: Negative correlations were observed between the percentage of intact HIV DNA and the frequencies of bifunctional HIV peptide-stimulated CD4 T cells (IL-2+TNFα+ and IFNγ+IL-2+).
source: Interestingly, for the percentage of intact HIV DNA, negative correlations were observed with the frequencies of set subsets of bifunctional HIV peptide-stimulated CD4 T cells (IL-2+TNFα+ and IFN γ+IL-2+), as well as with years on ART.
evidence: The manuscript reports negative correlations between percentage intact HIV DNA and specific HIV-specific T cell responses.

claim: The magnitude of correlation with immune parameters was typically stronger for total HIV DNA compared to intact HIV DNA.
source: Notably, the magnitude of correlation with immune parameters was typically stronger for total HIV DNA compared to intact HIV DNA (Table 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this comparative observation with reference to Table 2.

claim: CD127− CD4 T cell frequencies were significantly positively correlated with intact but not total HIV DNA.
source: A notable exception to this pattern was CD127− CD4 T cell frequencies, which were significantly positively correlated with intact but not total HIV DNA.
evidence: The manuscript reports a specific correlation pattern unique to CD127 expression.

claim: Larger HIV reservoirs are associated with increased levels of immune activation and depletion of the naive T cell compartment.
source: Overall these findings support the notion that larger HIV reservoirs are associated with increased levels of immune activation and depletion of the naive T cell compartment.
evidence: The manuscript draws this inference from multiple correlations observed in the data.

claim: CD127 expression on CD4 T cells is uniquely associated with the intact reservoir rather than the total reservoir.
source: Furthermore, the data indicate that there may be some immune features, such as CD127 expression on CD4 T cells that are uniquely associated with the intact reservoir rather than the total reservoir.
evidence: The manuscript infers this unique association from the differential correlation patterns observed.

claim: Age and race emerged as important covariates of several immunophenotypes related to T cell subsets, particularly the naive and central memory compartments, as well as KLRG1.
source: Across all three analyses, age and race emerged as an important covariate of several immunophenotypes related to T cell subsets, particularly the naive and central memory compartments, as well as KLRG1, a marker of immune senescence (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from LOCO inference analysis identifying important covariates.

claim: Biological sex was a key variable for model prediction of NK cell NKG2A expression.
source: Interestingly, biological sex was a key variable for model prediction of NK cell NKG2A expression, and race was important for Tem CD8, KLRG1+/CD27+ CD8 frequency for all three models.
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from LOCO inference analysis identifying biological sex as important for specific predictions.

claim: Race was important for Tem CD8 and KLRG1+/CD27+ CD8 frequency for all three models.
source: Interestingly, biological sex was a key variable for model prediction of NK cell NKG2A expression, and race was important for Tem CD8, KLRG1+/CD27+ CD8 frequency for all three models.
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from LOCO inference analysis identifying race as important for specific predictions.

claim: Total HIV DNA frequency was an important model input for prediction of PD-1+ CD4 T naive cells, HIV-specific IL-2+TNFα−IFNγ−CD107−CD4 T cells, and CD4/CD8 T cell frequencies.
source: Total HIV DNA frequency was an important model input for prediction of PD-1+ CD4 T naive cells, HIV-specific IL-2+TNFα−IFNγ−CD107−CD4 T cells, and CD4/CD8 T cell frequencies, among others (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from LOCO inference analysis identifying total HIV DNA as important for specific predictions.

claim: Total HIV DNA frequency and intact HIV DNA frequency were important predictors of CD4 T effector memory HLA-DR+CD38+ expression.
source: Total HIV DNA frequency and intact HIV DNA frequency were also important predictors of CD4 T effector memory HLA-DR+CD38+ expression (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from LOCO inference analysis identifying both total and intact HIV DNA as important predictors.

claim: The percentage of intact HIV DNA did not appear to contribute greatly to the predictive power of the model for the variance in the immunophenotypes examined.
source: The percentage of intact HIV DNA did not appear to contribute greatly to the predictive power of the model for the variance in the immunophenotypes examined (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), most likely due to its relatively high correlation with years of ART.
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from LOCO inference analysis and provides a speculative explanation.

claim: The most effective individual immune markers for classification of high versus low total HIV DNA frequency included %NKG2A+CD4 T (AUC = 0.70), %PD-1+Tn CD4 T (AUC = 0.68), and %CD38+/HLA-DR− CD8 T (AUC = 0.68).
source: The most effective individual immune markers for classification of high versus low total HIV DNA frequency included %NKG2A+CD4 T (AUC = 0.70), %PD-1+Tn CD4 T (AUC = 0.68), and %CD38+/HLA-DR− CD8 T (AUC = 0.68).
evidence: The manuscript reports specific AUC values from ROC curve analysis.

claim: The most effective markers for classifying based on the frequency of intact HIV DNA frequency included %CD127+ CD4 T (AUC = 0.71), %CD8 T (AUC = 0.66), and %Tn CD8 T (AUC = 0.65).
source: In contrast, the most effective markers for classifying based on the frequency of intact HIV DNA frequency included %CD127+ CD4 T (AUC = 0.71), %CD8 T (AUC = 0.66), and %Tn CD8 T (AUC = 0.65).
evidence: The manuscript reports specific AUC values from ROC curve analysis.

claim: For percentage intact HIV DNA, years of ART (AUC = 0.72), %CD107−IFNγ−IL-2+TNFα+ CD4 T (AUC = 0.65) and %KLRG1+/PD1+ CD4 T (AUC = 0.65) were the most effective markers.
source: Finally, for percentage intact HIV DNA, years of ART (AUC = 0.72), %CD107−IFNγ−IL-2+TNFα+ CD4 T (AUC = 0.65) and %KLRG1+/PD1+ CD4 T (AUC = 0.65) were the most effective (Figure 3).
evidence: The manuscript reports specific AUC values from ROC curve analysis.

claim: There were more variables that had AUC values >0.6 for total reservoir frequency (44 variables) than for intact reservoir (19 variables) and percent intact (23 variables).
source: Similar to the findings in the Spearman correlations (Table 2) and LOCO inference analysis (Figure 2), there were more variables that had AUC values >0.6 for total reservoir frequency (Supplementary file 1i): 44 variables above this threshold for the total reservoir, but only 19 variables for the intact reservoir and 23 variables for percent intact.
evidence: The manuscript reports counts of variables meeting a specific AUC threshold.

claim: Two distinct clusters of PWH were identified using PaCMAP dimension reduction with total HIV DNA-associated features.
source: Interestingly, while no clear clustering was observed when we use intact reservoir frequency or percentage intact HIV DNA-associated features, we observed two distinct clusters of PWH (clusters 1 and 2, Figure 4A) when using total HIV DNA-associated features.
evidence: The manuscript reports findings from unsupervised dimension reduction analysis.

claim: Cluster 1 contained 50 participants and cluster 2 contained 65 participants.
source: These clusters were of roughly equal size with 50 participants in cluster 1 and 65 in cluster 2.
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of participants in each cluster.

claim: Cluster 1 is characterized by a smaller total HIV reservoir frequency, but greater percentage of intact proviruses.
source: Analysis of quantitative reservoir frequencies across clusters (Figure 4C–E) demonstrated that cluster 1 is characterized by a smaller total HIV reservoir frequency, but greater percentage of intact proviruses (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The manuscript reports characteristics of cluster 1 from quantitative analysis.

claim: Cluster 2 is defined by a larger total reservoir frequency, but lower percentage of intact proviruses.
source: In contrast, cluster 2 is defined by a larger total reservoir frequency, but lower percentage of intact proviruses (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The manuscript reports characteristics of cluster 2 from quantitative analysis.

claim: Cluster 2 was associated with a lower fraction of naive CD4 and CD8 T cells.
source: Cluster 2, which had a higher total and intact absolute reservoir frequency but lower percentage of intact proviruses, was associated with a lower fraction of naive CD4 and CD8 T cells.
evidence: The manuscript reports immune characteristics distinguishing cluster 2.

claim: Cluster 2 had generally higher expression of immune exhaustion markers, including KLRG1 and PD-1.
source: Additionally, cluster 2 had generally higher expression of immune exhaustion markers, including KLRG1 and PD-1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports immune characteristics distinguishing cluster 2.

claim: Cluster 2 had an older median age, longer time on ART, lower CD4 nadir, and lower current CD4 T cell count.
source: Notably, with regard to other clinical variables, cluster 2 had an older median age, longer time on ART, lower CD4 nadir, and lower current CD4 T cell count (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports clinical characteristics distinguishing cluster 2.

claim: Cannabis users were enriched in cluster 1, which had lower levels of immune exhaustion markers.
source: Interestingly, a subset of participants in this study had clinical data regarding CB use. CB users were enriched in cluster 1, which had lower levels of immune exhaustion markers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports an association between cannabis use and cluster membership.

claim: A decision tree for total HIV DNA frequency achieved 83.5% accuracy using only four immune variables: CD8 T cell frequency, CD4 nadir, %CD38+HLA-DR− CD8 T cells, and %NKG2A+ CD4 T cells.
source: For the total HIV DNA frequency decision tree, only four immune variables were required to accurately describe high versus low total HIV DNA status (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1): CD8 T cell frequency, CD4 nadir, %CD38+HLA-DR− CD8 T cells, and %NKG2A+ CD4 T cells. The tree divided the cohort into five subgroups (leaves), among which three have high total reservoir frequency and two have low total reservoir frequency. Comparing the labels provided by GOSDT model with the actual data, the tree achieved 83.5%accuracy (i.e. misclassifying 19 PWH among the overall cohort of 115 PWH).
evidence: The manuscript reports the accuracy and variables used in the decision tree model.

claim: The decision tree for intact reservoir frequency achieved 82.6% accuracy.
source: We then repeated this approach for classifying the cohort participants with respect to intact reservoir frequency (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2). Despite the overall lower correlation between the immune cell phenotypes and the intact reservoir size, this tree nevertheless achieved 82.6%accuracy.
evidence: The manuscript reports the accuracy of the decision tree model for intact reservoir.

claim: The decision tree for percentage intact HIV DNA achieved 82.4% accuracy.
source: Finally, a third iteration of GOSDT generation was performed, classifying the cohort participants with respect to percentage intact of total proviruses (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 3). This tree achieved 82.4%accuracy and relied on years of ART treatment, %KLRG1+ CD27 CD4 T cells, %CD127+ CD4 T cells, and recent clinical CD4 count.
evidence: The manuscript reports the accuracy and variables used in the decision tree model for percentage intact.

claim: Logistic Regression achieved the highest mean classification accuracy (69.31%) for total reservoir frequency in test data.
source: Overall, we found that for total reservoir frequency, LR achieved highest mean classification accuracy (69.31%) in test data.
evidence: The manuscript reports the performance of machine learning models on test data.

claim: Logistic Regression models performed best for predicting intact reservoir frequency with average 65.17% test accuracy.
source: Similarly, LR models performed best for predicting intact reservoir frequency compared to other methods (average 65.17% test accuracy, see Figure 6C).
evidence: The manuscript reports the performance of machine learning models on test data.

claim: Machine learning algorithms predicted with approximately 70% accuracy whether a given participant had qualitatively high or low levels of total or intact HIV DNA.
source: Overall, these analyses demonstrate that we can use ML tools to construct models that can predict with approximately 70% accuracy whether a given PWH has qualitatively low or high total HIV DNA frequency, intact HIV DNA frequency or percentage of HIV DNA.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the predictive accuracy of machine learning models.

claim: 69 host variables correlated (unadjusted p < 0.05) with one or more characteristics of the HIV reservoir.
source: For the initial analysis, Spearman correlation of the clinical–demographic and immunophenotypic data with HIV reservoir metrics was assessed. 69 host variables correlated (unadjusted p < 0.05) with one or more characteristics of the HIV reservoir (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of variables with significant unadjusted correlations.

claim: Following Benjamini–Hochberg p-value adjustment for multiple comparisons using a false discovery rate correction at 5%, 31 variables were found to be correlated with total HIV DNA, 3 with intact HIV DNA, and 4 with the percentage of intact HIV DNA.
source: Following Benjamini–Hochberg p-value adjustment for multiple comparisons using a false discovery rate correction at 5%, 31 variables were found to be correlated with total HIV DNA, 3 with intact HIV DNA, and 4 with the percentage of intact HIV DNA (Table 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of variables with significant adjusted correlations after multiple comparison correction.

claim: The correlations observed were generally weak to moderate in magnitude (the mean of the absolute values of Spearman correlation coefficients was 0.31 for total HIV DNA, 0.33 for intact HIV DNA, and 0.35 for percent intact HIV DNA).
source: Of note, the correlations observed were generally weak to moderate in magnitude (the mean of the absolute values of Spearman correlation coefficients was 0.31 for total HIV DNA, 0.33 for intact HIV DNA, and 0.35 for percent intact HIV DNA).
evidence: The manuscript reports the mean magnitude of correlation coefficients.

claim: No significant differences in the reservoir based on biological sex or race were observed.
source: No significant differences in the reservoir based on biological sex or race were observed (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: The manuscript reports the absence of significant differences in reservoir by sex or race.

claim: The advent of antiretroviral therapy (ART) has significantly decreased morbidity and mortality associated with HIV infection.
source: The advent of antiretroviral therapy (ART) has significantly decreased morbidity and mortality associated with HIV infection.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the impact of ART on HIV outcomes.

claim: A long-lived proviral reservoir precludes a cure of HIV infection.
source: However, a long-lived proviral reservoir precludes a cure of infection (Finzi et al., 1997; Chun et al., 1997; Chun et al., 1998; Wong et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to foundational studies on the HIV reservoir.

claim: The largest and most well-characterized HIV reservoir is within CD4 T cells.
source: While a number of cell types have been proposed as contributing to the HIV reservoir, the largest and most well-characterized reservoir is within CD4 T cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the HIV persistence field.

claim: The HIV reservoir is comprised of a heterogeneous mixture of full-length replication-competent proviruses and a larger set of defective proviruses containing internal deletions or APOBEC-mediated hypermutation(s).
source: Molecular analyses of residual HIV proviruses in CD4 T cells during ART have shown that the reservoir is comprised of a heterogeneous mixture of full-length replication-competent proviruses and a larger set of defective proviruses containing internal deletions or APOBEC-mediated hypermutation(s) (Ho et al., 2013; Imamichi et al., 2016; Bruner et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to molecular studies characterizing the HIV reservoir.

claim: Infected cells can undergo clonal expansion and contraction over time in response to homeostatic cues or antigen-driven activation.
source: Infected cells can undergo clonal expansion and contraction over time in response to homeostatic cues or antigen-driven activation (Maldarelli et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2018; Collora et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on clonal dynamics of infected cells.

claim: People with HIV (PWH) on therapy exhibit a persistent level of T cell immune activation and other altered phenotypes compared to uninfected individuals.
source: In addition to the presence of a latent HIV reservoir, people with HIV (PWH) on therapy exhibit a persistent level of T cell immune activation and other altered phenotypes compared to uninfected individuals, involving cells of both the innate and adaptive immune systems (Sponaugle et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review on immune activation in PWH.

claim: HIV infection is associated with increased levels of inflammatory biomarkers and increased immune cell activation.
source: Specifically, HIV infection is associated with increased levels of inflammatory biomarkers and increased immune cell activation (Hunt et al., 2003; Bastard et al., 2012; Kottilil et al., 2006; Lichtfuss et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on inflammation and immune activation in HIV.

claim: PWH exhibit a depleted naive T cell compartment.
source: PWH also exhibit a depleted naive T cell compartment (Prescott, 1995) and increased expression of activation/exhaustion and senescence markers such as CD38, PD-1, and KLRG1 (Day et al., 2006; Ibegbu et al., 2005; Tavenier et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2020; Hatano et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on T cell compartment changes in HIV.

claim: PWH exhibit increased expression of activation/exhaustion and senescence markers such as CD38, PD-1, and KLRG1.
source: PWH also exhibit a depleted naive T cell compartment (Prescott, 1995) and increased expression of activation/exhaustion and senescence markers such as CD38, PD-1, and KLRG1 (Day et al., 2006; Ibegbu et al., 2005; Tavenier et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2020; Hatano et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies on immune markers in HIV.

claim: The molecular mechanisms underlying persistent immune activation and dysfunction for PWH on ART are unclear.
source: The molecular mechanisms underlying persistent immune activation and dysfunction for PWH on ART are unclear, but it is possible that ongoing viral gene expression and reverse transcription generates ligands for pattern recognition receptors in the innate immune system (Alter et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that the mechanisms are unclear and provides a speculative explanation.

claim: Ongoing viral gene expression and reverse transcription may generate ligands for pattern recognition receptors in the innate immune system.
source: The molecular mechanisms underlying persistent immune activation and dysfunction for PWH on ART are unclear, but it is possible that ongoing viral gene expression and reverse transcription generates ligands for pattern recognition receptors in the innate immune system (Alter et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript speculates about a possible mechanism with citation support.

claim: Persistent sequelae of the massive disruptions to T cell homeostasis, intestinal permeability, and lymphoid structures that occur during untreated HIV infection may cause ongoing immune activation during ART.
source: However, another important potential cause of ongoing immune activation during ART is persistent sequelae of the massive disruptions to T cell homeostasis, intestinal permeability, and lymphoid structures that occur during untreated HIV infection (Lederman et al., 2013; Heather et al., 2015; Hunt et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript speculates about another possible mechanism with citation support.

claim: The HIV reservoir and the host immune system may interact in multiple complex ways during therapy.
source: It is possible that the HIV reservoir and the host immune system interact in multiple complex ways during therapy.
evidence: The manuscript speculates about the nature of reservoir-immune system interactions.

claim: Previous studies have identified several activation/exhaustion markers that correlate with total HIV DNA, including the CD4/CD8 ratio, T cell expression of HLA-DR, CD38, PD-1, CTLA-4, and LAG-3, and NK cell KLRG1 expression.
source: These studies have identified several activation/exhaustion markers that correlate with total HIV DNA, including the CD4/CD8 ratio, T cell expression of HLA-DR, CD38, PD-1, CTLA-4, and LAG-3, and NK cell KLRG1 expression.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes findings from previous studies in the field.

claim: Not all studies have found associations of total HIV DNA with immune subsets, particularly for CD4 T cell HLA-DR and CD38 expression during long-term ART.
source: However, not all studies have found associations of total HIV DNA and immune subsets, particularly for CD4 T cell HLA-DR and CD38 expression (Poizot-Martin et al., 2013; Gandhi et al., 2017; Gálvez et al., 2021; Besson et al., 2014) during long-term ART.
evidence: The manuscript cites studies that did not find certain associations.

claim: The size of the HIV reservoir has been linked to the abundance of specific bacteria species in the intestinal microbiome.
source: Specifically, the size of the reservoir has been linked to the abundance of specific bacteria species in the intestinal microbiome (Borgognone et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study linking reservoir size to microbiome composition.

claim: Genetic studies have indicated the existence of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that are associated with reservoir size, including SNPs in MX1 and IRF7.
source: Also, genetic studies have indicated the existence of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that are associated with reservoir size, including SNPs in MX1 and IRF7 (Siegel et al., 2023; Thorball et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites genetic studies identifying SNPs associated with reservoir size.

claim: Recent studies indicate enrichment of the intact HIV reservoir in cells expressing VLA-4, but no correlation with classic T cell activation markers.
source: Recent studies indicate enrichment of the intact HIV reservoir in cells expressing VLA-4, but no correlation with classic T cell activation markers (Dufour et al., 2023; Horsburgh et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites recent studies on intact reservoir characteristics.

claim: Most previous studies were not able to distinguish intact proviruses from defective proviruses, making the relationship between the immune system and the intact reservoir unclear.
source: One important limitation of most of these studies is that they were not able to distinguish intact proviruses from defective proviruses, making the relationship between the immune system and the intact reservoir unclear.
evidence: The manuscript identifies a limitation of previous studies in the field.

claim: There is a recent, growing appreciation for the profound influence of ART initiation timing and length of treatment on the size and composition of the HIV reservoir.
source: Finally, there is a recent, growing appreciation for the profound influence of ART initiation timing and length of treatment on the size and composition of the HIV reservoir that must be accounted for in assessing persistent immune activation in PWH on therapy (Siliciano and Siliciano, 2022; Sponaugle et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites recent reviews highlighting the importance of treatment timing.

claim: The correlation of NKG2A expression in CD4 T cells with the total reservoir size represents a novel observation.
source: The correlation of NKG2A expression in CD4 T cells with the total reservoir size represents a novel observation that merits further investigation.
evidence: The manuscript identifies this as a novel finding from the current study.

claim: Only a very small percentage of CD4 T cells express NKG2A (less than 1%).
source: Only a very small percentage of CD4 T cells express NKG2A (less at 1%), and the biological significance for the correlation of these cells with the HIV reservoir is unknown.
evidence: The manuscript reports the frequency of NKG2A+ CD4 T cells.

claim: NKG2A is known to function as an inhibitory receptor for NK cells and for CD8 T cells, but its role in CD4 T cells is less clear.
source: NGK2A is known to function as an inhibitory receptor for NK cells and for CD8 T cells, but its role in CD4 T cells is less clear (Creelan and Antonia, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript cites knowledge about NKG2A function with a citation.

claim: The stronger relationship between immune cell phenotypes and the total reservoir, rather than the intact reservoir, could be driven by the more numerous defective proviruses promoting inflammation or immune activation through innate immune sensing pathways.
source: The stronger relationship between the immune cell phenotypes and the total reservoir, rather than the intact reservoir, should be investigated further. We speculate that this association could be driven by the more numerous defective proviruses promoting inflammation or immune activation through innate immune sensing pathways, or a greater level of transcriptional activity for defective proviruses.
evidence: The manuscript speculates about a possible mechanism for the observed pattern.

claim: Defective proviruses may have a greater level of transcriptional activity.
source: The stronger relationship between the immune cell phenotypes and the total reservoir, rather than the intact reservoir, should be investigated further. We speculate that this association could be driven by the more numerous defective proviruses promoting inflammation or immune activation through innate immune sensing pathways, or a greater level of transcriptional activity for defective proviruses.
evidence: The manuscript speculates about a possible mechanism for the observed pattern.

claim: The stronger association of total proviral burden with immunophenotype may reflect persistent damage caused to the immune system before therapy, and this association may not result from ongoing interactions between HIV and the immune system during therapy.
source: It is important to note, however, that it is also possible that the stronger association of total proviral burden with immunophenotype reflects persistent damage caused to the immune system before therapy, and that this association between the total reservoir and immune cells may not result from ongoing interactions between HIV and the immune system during therapy.
evidence: The manuscript presents an alternative speculative explanation for the observed associations.

claim: CD127 is the alpha-chain IL-7 receptor and is expressed on long-lived memory T cells that are depleted during untreated HIV infection.
source: CD127 is the alpha-chain IL-7 receptor and is expressed on long-lived memory T cells that are depleted during untreated HIV infection.
evidence: The manuscript provides background knowledge about CD127.

claim: Post-ART, the frequency of CD127+ memory CD4 subsets in PWH increases over time, albeit slowly.
source: Post-ART, the frequency of CD127+ memory CD4 subsets in PWH increases over time, albeit slowly (Sponaugle et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study on CD127+ cell dynamics during ART.

claim: CD127+ cells are enriched in latent HIV infection in tissues.
source: Interestingly, CD127+ cells are enriched in latent HIV infection in tissues (Hsiao et al., 2020), and IL-7 is associated with slower natural reservoir decay (Chomont et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies on CD127+ cells and HIV reservoir.

claim: IL-7 is associated with slower natural reservoir decay.
source: Interestingly, CD127+ cells are enriched in latent HIV infection in tissues (Hsiao et al., 2020), and IL-7 is associated with slower natural reservoir decay (Chomont et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study on IL-7 and reservoir decay.

claim: IL-7 signaling is known to drive expression of VLA-4.
source: Furthermore, IL-7 signaling is known to drive expression of VLA-4, which was recently reported to highly enrich for genetically intact, inducible proviruses (Dufour et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites knowledge about IL-7 signaling and a recent study on VLA-4.

claim: VLA-4 was recently reported to highly enrich for genetically intact, inducible proviruses.
source: Furthermore, IL-7 signaling is known to drive expression of VLA-4, which was recently reported to highly enrich for genetically intact, inducible proviruses (Dufour et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites a recent study on VLA-4 and intact proviruses.

claim: The two clusters identified may represent two proposed types of reservoirs: one type with smaller reservoirs enriched in Tcm cells and associated with lower levels of Ki67+ cells and immune activation, and another type with larger reservoirs enriched in Ttm cells and associated with higher levels of Ki67+ cells and immune activation.
source: These two clusters are also interesting in the context of a previous study examining reservoir characteristics which proposed two major types of viral reservoir within PWH: one type with smaller reservoirs that were enriched in Tcm cells and associated with lower levels of Ki67+ cells and immune activation, and another type with larger reservoirs that were enriched in Ttm cells and associated with higher levels of Ki67+ cells and immune activation (Chomont et al., 2009). It is possible that these two proposed types of reservoirs represent the two clusters we observe using immune markers and DR, although we were unable to examine the frequency of HIV proviruses specifically within Tcm and Ttm cells in this study.
evidence: The manuscript speculates about a connection to previous findings with citation support.
